text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chief justice rules certain information cannot be called "secret information" even if government chooses to treat it so, referring to case of lawyer who obtained addresses of people from a policeman.
- President Bill Clinton begins second term with call for U.S. leadership abroad and unity at home, in inaugural address setting tone for new administration.
- South Korean President Kim Young Sam offers compromise deal to end industrial strife over controversial labour law, but bid rejected by South Korean unions.
- Singapore's foreign direct investments in region exceed US$8 billion in 1995.
- Door maker Chuan Soon Huat IPO 52 times subscribed.
- Lung Kee Metal Holdings IPO 28 times subscribed.
- Contrary to earlier findings that Singapore's economic growth had been purely input-driven, new study shows efficiency gains had been main engine over last 25 years or so.
- Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gives upbeat assessment of U.S. economy, suggesting Fed's policy-making open market committee isn't likely to raise interest rates.
- Silent price war being waged by Mercedes-Benz retailers across Singapore, with authorised supplier trimming rates by about Singapore $20,000.
- Electronics stocks surge after government forecast of between 10 and 15 percent growth in electronics output this year.
- Singapore Telecom hopes to win Taiwan paging licence.
- Freight Links Express Holdings reports 41.5 percent jump in group net earnings to S$3 million for six months ended October 31, 1996.
